subject.title: Isolated cron consistently fails with "LLM request failed" on model-call-started phase

question: Should isolated cron treat setup-phase progress as enough to leave the 60-second pre-execution guard, and should repeated isolated-cron failures reset or rotate the run/session state after N errors?
rationale: Current main still has the setup-progress watchdog abort path, open PRs disagree on the exact phase boundary, and the latest report points to a session-state cascade that is not just a classifier or stream-stall timeout bug.

options.title: Revise and land the watchdog contract first
options.body: Preserve the runner-start no-progress guard, allow later setup/context phases to count as progress, and require focused plus live scheduled-cron proof before closing the broad issue.

options.title: Add session reset after repeated failures
options.body: Introduce an isolated-cron-only run/session reset after a small consecutive-error threshold with diagnostics, but only after maintainers accept that lifecycle behavior.

options.title: Wait for a fresh live repro before changing lifecycle
options.body: Keep current retry/backoff behavior and ask affected users for redacted current-main logs before adding a reset or changing timeout semantics beyond the narrowed watchdog fix.

recommendation.title: Revise and land the watchdog contract first
recommendation.body: Preserve the runner-start no-progress guard, allow later setup/context phases to count as progress, and require focused plus live scheduled-cron proof before closing the broad issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is about the cron watchdog/session lifecycle contract, and steipete has the strongest sampled feature-history signal in the implicated cron phase and runner paths.
